title: The dog's first swim
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The dog goes off the dock after a gull. He has never been in water past the ankle. He swims like he's done it forever, which is how he does everything. Gully hauls him out by the scruff. Wood draws the wavy kelp line for real this time.

panels.composition: The dock. BARNABY at the edge, rigid, a gull on the water. WOOD too far back. GULLY coiling rope.

image.prompt: a small dog rigid at a dock's edge watching a gull on the water, a young man too far away, a teenager coiling rope, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The dog in the air. Off the dock. Four strokes, and none of them touching anything.

image.prompt: a small dog mid-leap off a dock over gray water, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The dog swimming, head up, as if he'd always. The gull gone. Gully flat on the dock reaching down.

image.prompt: a small dog swimming with its head up below a dock while a teenager lies flat reaching down for it, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The dog on the dock, soaked, shaking, the wavy line rising off him. Kelp, this time. Wood drawing it as fast as it happens.

image.prompt: a soaked small dog shaking itself on a dock with wavy lines rising from its coat, a young man drawing, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The kelp line, earned. He swims like he's done it forever.
